# Byte Promotions and Signed Comparisons

## Exact contract and predictions

The selected byte is `(incoming >> (8 * (initial & 7))) & 255`. Its eight bits
are copied into an exact-width int8_t object. The threshold is
`((initial >> 8) & 255) - 128`, calculated as an int. Outputs are the byte index,
the signed value encoded as a uint64_t, the unsigned value, and the signed and
unsigned-byte comparison results (each 0 or 1). The header requires eight-bit
bytes and a 32-bit int. All inputs are unsigned 64-bit values.

Both byte types promote to int for these comparisons because int represents
their complete ranges. A uint8_t operand therefore does not make this comparison
an unsigned-int comparison. The signed byte retains its negative value; the
unsigned byte has a value from 0 to 255. The provided C code separates the source
bit representation from the comparison. It does not convert an out-of-range
unsigned value to a signed integer by a cast.

The default inputs 8007 and 80ff7f0100fe0281 select byte 80 with threshold 0.
The five output words are:

`0000000000000007 ffffffffffffff80 0000000000000080 0000000000000001 0000000000000000`

`--changed` uses two zero inputs: the threshold is -128, and all five words are
zero. Also predict bytes 7f, 80 and ff at thresholds -1, 0 and 127. In a separate
reference copy replace the signed helper's comparison with
`return (uint8_t)value < threshold;`. This is a defined conversion but changes
the contract for negative signed bytes. Record a rejected case and a case that
still agrees. Keep the unsigned helper and model unchanged.

## Working baseline and observation task

Both role programs already work. Complete analysis.md with predictions and real
compiler/debugger evidence. The separate reference supplies portable reasoning;
its addresses and machine instruction choices must be recorded from the current
build. The required Unit 9 score project follows one arithmetic function through
the toolchain; this optional investigation examines the stated type or alias
contract across optimization levels.

Use ordinary-user Linux x86-64, the System V AMD64 ABI, C17, Clang or GCC,
CMake 3.20+, GDB and binutils. On macOS use an x86-64 Linux lab/VM; on Windows use
an x86-64 WSL distribution. Each role contains baseline.c, operation.c, main.c,
lab.h, model.c, tests.c, abi_checks.S, CMakeLists.txt and analysis.md. The roles
differ only in analysis.md. Keep README.md one level above the selected role.

baseline.c contains the inspected functions. operation.c calls them from a
separate translation unit, without link-time optimization, so actual function
entry and return observations remain available in both builds. model.c checks
the same five-word contract through independent arithmetic. tests.c also calls
the supplied six-register ABI probe; explicit checks remain active in Release.

From the selected role directory:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-O0 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG="-O0 -g"
cmake --build build-O0 --verbose --parallel 1
ctest --test-dir build-O0 --output-on-failure
./build-O0/app
./build-O0/app --changed
cmake -S . -B build-O2 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE="-O2 -g -DNDEBUG"
cmake --build build-O2 --verbose --parallel 1
ctest --test-dir build-O2 --output-on-failure
mkdir -p observed
clang -std=c17 -O0 -g -S -masm=intel -fverbose-asm baseline.c -o observed/baseline-O0.s
clang -std=c17 -O2 -g -S -masm=intel -fverbose-asm baseline.c -o observed/baseline-O2.s
objdump -d -M intel build-O0/app > observed/linked-O0.txt
objdump -d -M intel build-O2/app > observed/linked-O2.txt
gdb ./build-O0/app
```

Repeat with GCC in separate build directories, recording `clang --version` or `gcc --version` and
all flags. The two source listings are assembler input, whereas objdump shows
the linked program's instructions and addresses. Comments and directives are
not executed instructions. The ordinary contracts check 10,269 fixed and
deterministic pairs. Additional native verification compares actual result rows
with a Python integer/owned-object model and assembles and executes the generated
listings. Unsupported app arguments exit 64; a changed-contract mismatch exits 78.

## Independent input cases

`contracts --rows` accepts pairs of unsigned hexadecimal tokens, each one to
sixteen digits without a sign or 0x prefix. Whitespace separates tokens. Each
output row contains the ABI preservation flag (1 means the six saved registers
were preserved) followed by the five actual hexadecimal result words. Compare
those words with the predictions; row mode reports observations rather than
grading the worksheet. Malformed, oversized or incomplete token pairs exit 64.

```sh
printf '8000 80\n8000 ff\nff00 7f\n' | ./build-O0/contracts --rows
```

In GDB set disassembly-flavor intel and break at the inspected function's entry.
Record actual argument widths, PC, RSP and the return word at entry, then step
its instructions through RET. Verify the returned value at the declared width,
the caller PC and RSP after return. For pointer functions record both valid owned
addresses and the pointed-to words before/after stores. Repeat on the optimized
binary; do not copy addresses or assume source-line stepping has the same shape.

Retain TARGET, PREDICT, TYPES, MAP, OPTIMIZE, TRACE and REGRESSION evidence in
analysis.md. Keep the provided C and ABI code unchanged outside the separate
controlled-regression copy. Test success does not complete the observation task.

References: [WG14 C draft N1570](https://open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf),
sections 6.3.1.1, 6.3.1.3, 6.7.3.1 and 7.20.1.1. The project compiles as C17.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(CompilerObservationLab LANGUAGES C ASM)
if(NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux" OR NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(x86_64|amd64|AMD64)$")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Use Linux x86-64 with the System V AMD64 ABI.")
endif()
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION FALSE)
add_executable(app main.c model.c operation.c baseline.c)
add_executable(contracts tests.c model.c abi_checks.S operation.c baseline.c)
foreach(target IN ITEMS app contracts)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic;-Wconversion;-Werror>")
endforeach()
enable_testing()
add_test(NAME compiler_observation_contract COMMAND contracts)

# Byte Promotions and Signed Comparisons: observations

## TARGET

The target is ordinary-user Linux x86-64 and the System V AMD64 ABI. The header requires eight-bit exact-width byte types and a 32-bit int. The CMake role build sets C17 and disables interprocedural optimization. Separate translation units preserve calls to the two inspected helpers while allowing their bodies to optimize. Use the exact commands in README.md and retain the current compiler version; the reference does not supply another machine's addresses.

## PREDICT

Default index7 selects byte80: signed -128, unsigned128, threshold0. The five words are 0000000000000007 ffffffffffffff80 0000000000000080 0000000000000001 0000000000000000. Zero inputs select byte0 and threshold -128, giving five zero words. At threshold -1, signed/unsigned results for 7f,80,ff are (0,0),(1,0),(0,0). At threshold0 they are (0,0),(1,0),(1,0); at127 they are (0,0),(1,0),(1,0). Equality uses strict less-than, so signed -1 is not less than -1.

## TYPES

The helper parameters are int8_t/int and uint8_t/int. The byte operands promote to int, preserving their respective values. The full int range includes every uint8_t value. Thus the unsigned byte's comparison can still use a signed int condition. memcpy transfers one valid byte representation into int8_t; the signed output is then converted to uint64_t modulo 2^64. The masked index bounds the shift to0..56 and the threshold stays in -128..127.

## MAP

Locate compiled_signed_compare and compiled_unsigned_compare in actual baseline-O0.s/baseline-O2.s and the linked listing. Their first arguments use only the low byte of the integer argument register; the threshold is an int, and the return is an int boolean in EAX. Upper argument-register bits are not the byte value contract. Find actual sign/zero extensions and compare operands before interpreting branch or SETcc mnemonics. Generated directives and debug records are not executed operations.

## OPTIMIZE

A build may remove the frame and stack-spilled parameters, keeping the widened byte and threshold in registers. The signed-byte value remains negative for80..ff; the unsigned-byte value remains0..255. The true/false results and five-word output must remain equal at both levels. An opcode or shorter instruction count is not a C guarantee. Compare the two listings from the same compiler, then repeat separately with GCC or Clang.

## TRACE

For the default, break at each helper entry. Record the actual low argument byte80 and int threshold0. Step the current instructions through RET: signed comparison returns int1, unsigned comparison int0. Check only the declared int return width, and verify actual caller PC/RSP against the saved entry return word and stack. Repeat with the optimized executable and retain its own addresses and sequence.

## REGRESSION

Changing only the signed helper to return (uint8_t)value < threshold gives false for signed -128 versus0, although the supplied contract requires true. The default and unchanged contracts reject it. Zero inputs still agree because0 is not below -128. A second counterexample is signed -1 versus0. The controlled cast is defined C; its changed meaning is the error, not undefined behavior.

# Pointer Aliasing and Reload Decisions

## Exact contract and predictions

The ordinary helper adds delta to `*left`, XORs the resulting `*left` into
`*right`, and returns the final `*left`. Arithmetic is uint64_t modulo 2^64.
The restricted helper has the same statements with two restrict-qualified
pointer parameters. Its callers must supply distinct objects for this task,
which reads and modifies both objects. No test violates that requirement.

The operation owns two independent two-word arrays, each initially
`{initial, incoming}`. The ordinary helper uses the first array: left is slot 0,
right is slot 0 when initial is odd or slot 1 when initial is even, and delta is
incoming. The restricted helper always uses the two distinct slots of the
second array. Inputs are integers, never arbitrary addresses.

Outputs are the ordinary return, its final slot 0, its final slot 1, the restricted
return and its final right slot. For default inputs 3 and 5 the ordinary pointers
alias: 3 + 5 becomes 8, then 8 XOR 8 becomes 0; the untouched second slot remains 5.
The restricted call has separate objects: its return is 8 and right is5 XOR 8 = d.
The five hexadecimal words are:

`0000000000000000 0000000000000000 0000000000000005 0000000000000008 000000000000000d`

`--changed` uses 2 and 5, making the ordinary objects disjoint. Outputs are
`0000000000000007 0000000000000007 0000000000000002 0000000000000007 0000000000000002`.
Also predict zero, UINT64_MAX+1 wraparound and an odd initial with zero incoming.

The compiler must preserve the ordinary helper's behavior for both valid alias
patterns. The restricted call provides a stronger access contract and may allow
the compiler to retain a value across the right-hand store. Observe actual
reloads and store order at -O0 and -O2. Neither fewer instructions nor a particular
reload count is guaranteed. Equal pointers must never be passed to the restricted
helper in this task; sanitizer success would not validate that promise.

For the controlled regression, replace only the ordinary body in a disposable
reference copy with `uint64_t cached = *left + delta; *left = cached;
*right ^= cached; return cached;`. This remains defined C but returns the earlier
value after an aliased XOR. The default rejects it; the disjoint changed case
still agrees. The restricted helper and model remain unchanged.

# Pointer Aliasing and Reload Decisions: observations

## TARGET

The role is C17 on ordinary-user Linux x86-64 with eight-byte uint64_t objects and the System V AMD64 ABI. CMake builds baseline.c and operation.c separately without LTO. This keeps the inspected helper calls available while their bodies optimize. Record the actual target, compiler version and all flags using README.md; do not copy instruction addresses from another run.

## PREDICT

Default3,5 makes the ordinary arguments point to the same slot. The conceptual updates are3+5=8 and8 XOR8=0; the second slot stays5. The separate restricted call produces left8 and right13. Outputs are0,0,5,8,13. Changed2,5 uses distinct ordinary slots and yields7,7,2,7,2. Initial UINT64_MAX with incoming1 wraps the addition to0; as the initial is odd, the ordinary result is0 and untouched second slot1. Zero inputs give five zero words. The UINT64_MAX,1 case gives 0,0,1,0,1. Odd initial3 with incoming0 gives 0,0,0,3,3.

## TYPES

Each helper receives two valid uint64_t pointers and an unsigned delta. operation.c owns both arrays and fixes every pointer to one of their two slots. Ordinary calls support equal or distinct pointers. The restricted call always uses separate modified objects; an equal-pointer call would violate this task's access contract and is never executed. Unsigned addition and XOR have defined full-width behavior. Restrict does not insert a runtime test.

## MAP

Locate compiled_plain and compiled_restricted in actual generated and linked output. RDI/RSI hold the two object addresses and RDX the unsigned delta; RAX returns a full uint64_t. Follow actual eight-byte reads and stores, preserving whether the two addresses are equal. The ordinary return observes the final left object after the right store. A compiler may retain a value under the restricted contract, but the observed generated code decides whether it did so.

## OPTIMIZE

At -O0 there may be stack-spilled pointers and temporary values. At -O2 an ordinary helper must still work when its two pointers alias, whereas the restricted helper can rely on its caller obligation. Inspect actual reloads after the right store and any reordered stores. Intermediate nonvolatile memory operations need not correspond one-to-one with C source lines. The valid outputs, access domain and ABI remain the same; neither a specific reload count nor a speedup is guaranteed.

## TRACE

For the default ordinary call, record equal addresses and initial words3,3. Step its real instruction sequence and retain every selected owned-word state; final words and return are0. For the restricted call, record distinct addresses and initial3,5; final words are8,13 and return8. Verify both actual RET destinations and restored caller stack positions. Repeat on -O2 with fresh addresses. Sanitizer success cannot establish that every future caller respects restrict.

## REGRESSION

The cached-return replacement computes8 for the default, stores through the aliased right pointer to make the object0, then incorrectly returns the cached8. The unchanged contracts and default reject this defined-but-wrong body. Changed2,5 still returns7 and therefore cannot detect it. Keep both cases, the independent model and the restricted helper unchanged. Restore the supplied ordinary body after the disposable comparison.

if(NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux" OR NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(x86_64|amd64|AMD64)$")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Use Linux x86-64 with the System V AMD64 ABI.")
endif()
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION FALSE)
add_executable(app main.c model.c operation.c baseline.c)
add_executable(contracts tests.c model.c abi_checks.S operation.c baseline.c)
foreach(target IN ITEMS app contracts)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic;-Wconversion;-Werror>")
endforeach()
enable_testing()
add_test(NAME compiler_observation_contract COMMAND contracts)

#error "Use Linux x86-64 with the System V AMD64 ABI."
#endif
.intel_syntax noprefix
.text
.globl abi_probe
.type abi_probe, @function
abi_probe:
    push rbp
    push rbx
    push r12
    push r13
    push r14
    push r15
    sub rsp, 24
    mov rax, rdi
    mov QWORD PTR [rsp + 8], r8
    mov rdi, rsi
    mov rsi, rdx
    mov rdx, rcx
    mov rbx, 0x13579bdf2468ace0
    mov rbp, 0x2468ace013579bdf
    mov r12, 0x1122334455667788
    mov r13, 0x2233445566778899
    mov r14, 0x33445566778899aa
    mov r15, 0x445566778899aabb
    call rax
    mov r11, QWORD PTR [rsp + 8]
    mov DWORD PTR [r11], 0
    mov r10, 0x13579bdf2468ace0
    cmp rbx, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x2468ace013579bdf
    cmp rbp, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x1122334455667788
    cmp r12, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x2233445566778899
    cmp r13, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x33445566778899aa
    cmp r14, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov r10, 0x445566778899aabb
    cmp r15, r10
    jne .Lprobe_done
    mov DWORD PTR [r11], 1
.Lprobe_done:
    add rsp, 24
    pop r15
    pop r14
    pop r13
    pop r12
    pop rbx
    pop rbp
    ret
.size abi_probe, .-abi_probe
.section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits
